description: Portable, backend-neutral JavaScript ESM behavior fixtures for the in-process Deno sandbox. Sources are real ESM programs; this file records expected semantics but does not execute them. A future core/testkit facade decides how to realize each fixture.
executionNote: dev/validate-fixtures.py only validates JSON shape and static source bounds. No fixture source is executed and no runtime behavior is claimed.

cases.name: Global and prototype mutations stay inside one instance

procedure: Import the module in two fresh sandbox instances.
Read the default export from each instance.
Read a plain object's inherited property in each instance.
assertions: Both instances report globalCount 1; neither observes the other instance's mutation.
The prototype mutation is visible only inside the instance that made it.
A fresh instance sees an undefined __conformanceGlobal and an undefined __conformancePolluted.
The host global object and host prototypes are unchanged after both instances close.

cases.name: Module-level state is not shared across instances

procedure: Import the module in two fresh sandbox instances.
Call bump() twice on each instance's default export.
Read snapshot() from each instance.
assertions: Each instance evaluates the module exactly once.
Calling bump() in one instance never changes the other instance's count.
Re-importing within one instance reuses that instance's module cache; a separate instance gets a separate cache.
No module namespace object or mutable export is shared across instance boundaries.

cases.name: Static imports outside the allowed module graph are denied before evaluation

procedure: Attempt to load the module through the sandbox module loader.
Observe the load error and verify the default export was never evaluated.
assertions: At least one static specifier is rejected by the module loader; the exact first failing specifier is host-dependent.
The guest module body does not execute and no default export is produced.
Neither node:fs nor any file outside the allowed module root is resolved.
The rejection is reported as an authorization or module-resolution failure, not as a successful import of a stub.

cases.name: Dynamic import escape attempts reject without loading host modules

procedure: Import the module and allow its top-level await to settle.
Inspect every entry in the exported results array.
Verify no host file or network response was read and no child-process module was provided.
assertions: Every dynamic import rejects; none reports status loaded.
Computed relative specifiers do not bypass the module-root check.
file: URLs and remote HTTP specifiers are denied without network access.
node:child_process is either absent or rejected; no child process is created.
The guest cannot distinguish a missing module from a denied module in a way that reveals host filesystem entries.

cases.name: Guest process APIs cannot exit the host or reach native bindings

procedure: Import the module in a sandbox instance and read the report export.
Confirm the host process is still alive after the guest attempted process.exit(7).
Run a trivial host operation in a new instance to prove the host is responsive.
assertions: process is absent, or process.exit throws or is denied; it never terminates the host.
A successful return from process.exit is a failure of the sandbox, not an accepted outcome.
process.binding is unavailable or denied and returns no native binding object.
require is not a host-loading function; guest native addon loading is unavailable.
No subprocess, signal, or environment mutation is observed by the host.

cases.name: Native library and subprocess entry points are absent or denied

procedure: Import the module and read the probe report.
Verify no native library handle, PID, or child process was returned to the guest.
Confirm the host remains alive and can serve a subsequent operation.
assertions: Deno.dlopen, Deno.run, Deno.Command, and process.dlopen are absent or reject with an authorization error.
If a probed function exists only as a stub, calling it must not load a library or start a process.
No native symbol address, file descriptor, PID, or child handle is exposed to the guest.
Absence of the Deno global is a valid pass; the fixture must not require Deno-specific APIs to exist.

cases.name: A CPU-bound infinite loop is terminated at the deadline

procedure: Import the module with a 100 ms deadline.
Wait for the host to report timeout or termination.
Create and run a second fresh sandbox instance afterward.
Close the timed-out instance and verify its resources are released.
assertions: The operation is reported as timed out or terminated; it is not reported as success.
The host process remains alive and a subsequent fresh instance completes a trivial operation.
The endless loop cannot delay host shutdown indefinitely.
No result, partial export, or promise resolution from the timed-out instance is accepted.
Closing the instance is idempotent and releases its isolate and channels.

cases.name: A never-settling promise is bounded by the deadline

procedure: Import the module with a 200 ms deadline and allow event-loop turns to run.
Wait for the host to report timeout or termination.
Run a subsequent fresh instance and close the timed-out one.
assertions: Top-level await does not settle and the operation times out at the configured deadline.
The pending promise does not keep the host event loop alive after instance teardown.
The host remains responsive and a later fresh instance succeeds.
No value is accepted from the timed-out instance after cleanup.
Cleanup releases the instance's task queue and message channels without panicking.
